key_claims: Zwift training plans neglect Zone 1 and Zone 2 training, which are essential endurance building blocks for developing mitochondria and fat utilization

A rider using Zwift training plans for three seasons failed to improve on a local 8-10 minute climb segment, but improved by over 1.5 minutes in 8 weeks using a custom plan focused on zone-specific training
Zwift and Strava prioritize user acquisition and customer lifetime value through gamification (points, segments) rather than optimizing for actual athlete progression
Cardiac drift (heart rate rising while power stays constant during endurance rides) indicates poor endurance fitness and the need for more Zone 1-2 work before adding intensity
A proper training plan requires assessing fitness via threshold testing, establishing zones, understanding lifestyle constraints, and adjusting weekly based on feedback—not static gamified sessions
specific_numbers: 1.5 minutes improvement on segment over 8 weeks
200 watts at 120 beats per minute baseline
145 beats per minute end-of-session heart rate example (cardiac decoupling)
3 seasons of Zwift/Trainer Road training without improvement
cluster_reasoning: Episode critiques Zwift training plans and advocates for zone-specific training methodology, threshold testing, and periodised training—core coaching fundamentals that align directly with structured training and training metrics.
